qs.q: Which of the following periampullary tumours typically presents with earlier jaundice and a higher resectability rate compared to pancreatic head adenocarcinoma?
o: Ductal adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic body
Carcinoma of the ampulla of Vater
Neuroendocrine tumours of the islet cells
qs.e: Ampullary and duodenal tumours have a better prognosis because they present with earlier jaundice and higher resectability than pancreatic head cancer. Pancreatic body and tail tumours present much later and have a very low resectability rate.
qs.s: Pancreatic Head Cancer and Periampullary Tumours: Whipple Procedure: MCQs

qs.q: A 56-year-old woman undergoes a Whipple procedure for a resectable periampullary tumour. When designing the single jejunal limb reconstruction, which three anastomoses must be sequentially fashioned onto this limb?
qs.e: Reconstruction after a Whipple procedure involves a pancreaticojejunostomy, hepaticojejunostomy, and gastrojejunostomy on a single jejunal limb. Pancreaticogastrostomy is an alternative to pancreaticojejunostomy, but not part of the standard triple anastomosis sequence.
qs.s: Pancreatic Head Cancer and Periampullary Tumours: Whipple Procedure: MCQs

qs.q: A 70-year-old woman is evaluated in a high-volume surgical centre for a suspected periampullary tumour requiring a Whipple procedure. Provided the operation is performed by experienced multidisciplinary teams, what is her expected perioperative mortality rate?
qs.e: Perioperative mortality for a Whipple procedure is under 5% in high-volume centres. This low mortality rate reflects specialized surgical expertise and postoperative critical care management.
